title: Think Global, Design Local: Building Great Experiences for the People Behind the Product Presented by DoorDash, Inc.
description:
Product thinking doesn’t live in the product org. It lives wherever someone decides what an experience should feel like — and that includes the teams most people never think to call “product.” The office you walk into. The policy that meets you on your hardest day at work. The app setting that finally makes a screen readable.
In this session, leaders from Employee Relations, Workplace, and Data Science make the case that they’ve been shipping products all along. They’ll get specific about who their users really are, how they hear from the people whose needs are easiest to overlook, and what it takes to hold a global standard without flattening local reality — including how accessibility research led to Dark Mode on the DoorDash app, a quiet but meaningful win for low-vision users.
Come for the panel. Leave with a lens you can use Monday morning.

title: Access Unlocked: Presented by Microsoft's House of Black TechXcellence
description:
What could the right person, perspective or tool unlock for your next move? At Access Unlocked, watch three Next-Gen Makers take the stage with the career, business and creative challenges they’re navigating, while special guest advisors, including CultureCon CEO Imani Ellis, The Gathering Spot co-founder + CEO Ryan Wilson and Corporate It Girl Jodie Taylor, offer live feedback + solutions, hosted by Charles Beloved.
Then, step into the action yourself! Network with creators, founders, entrepreneurs and tech professionals, explore how Copilot can help move your work forward, and meet people who could unlock your next move. Whether you’re building, growing or figuring out what’s next, come ready to make progress on what matters to you. RSVP here.

title: Capital One Networking at AFROTECH™
description: Join Capital One for an exclusive networking experience where you’ll connect directly with their visionary executives, associates, chat with their recruiters and learn more about how they’re revolutionizing the future of technology. This event is by invitation only, visit their booth for more information.

title: AfroTech Legacy Dinner in partnership with Black Enterprise
description: A private, invite-only dinner celebrating the Future 50 2026 honorees and special guests, and commemorating 10 years of AfroTech. Hosted by Black Enterprise and sponsored by Nationwide.

title: Blavity In Black Presented By Sprite
description:
Blavity is turning up the volume on AfroTech's 10th anniversary. Blavity In Black is a signature event built around the soundtrack of the last decade a musical timeline moving through the songs, artists, and cultural moments that defined each era from 2016 to 2026.
Dress code: All Black, encouraged. Think formal, elevated, and expressive, come dressed to be part of the moment.
Get your tickets HERE: https://posh.vip/e/afrotech-conference-blavity-in-black

title: Executive Policy Breakfast Doors Open
HealthStack Continental Breakfast
Attendee Registration
description: The central hub for AfroTech badge pick-ups. Attendees can also get assistance with schedule access, venue navigation, and general event questions.

title: Executive Policy Breakfast
description:
Join us for the first ever AfroTech Policy Breakfast. We are gathering together some of the top  minds in social justice, civic engagement and public leadership to trade notes and empower one another. The decisions that will define the next decade of technology are being made by major companies and this is an opportunity for our public leaders to connect with them.
AfroTech is taking place during an election week, and it will be Forty-eight hours after the mid terms, this will be an opportunity for us to debrief the results and plan what is happening next.
Participants include mayors and members of Congress, chief executives and senior operators from the companies building artificial intelligence, healthcare, and financial infrastructure, and research directors from the institutions shaping the terms of the debate.
Attendance is by RSVP only. RSVP here:(https://posh.vip/e/afrotech-policy-breakfast)

title: Building AI Agents for Enterprise
description: This is a session for developers and people leaders. Build a foundational AI agent that securely interacts with your company's data and MCPs.  Bring your real questions and scenarios to AfroTech's AI Edge.

title: Expand Your Personal Tech Stack
description: Live Workshop identifying your current workflows and which AI tool to use wear to 10x your productivity and output at Work.

title: AI, Health Equity, and Brand Responsibility Presented by Planned Parenthood

speakers.name: Kevin Williams
speakers.title: Vice President, Digital Strategy & Experience External Affairs
speakers.company: Planned Parenthood Federation of America Planned Parenthood Action Fund

speakers.name: Cheryl Contee
speakers.title: Co-Founder
speakers.company: BrightWorks AI and Change Agent AI

description: As artificial intelligence rapidly transforms healthcare, organizations face important questions about innovation, ethics, access, and trust. In this fireside chat, Planned Parenthood will explore the opportunities AI presents for expanding health information and care, alongside the risks of bias, misinformation, privacy concerns, and unequal access. Together, we'll discuss the moral responsibility brands have to engage in these conversations, advocate for equitable outcomes, and help shape a future where technology serves all communities—not just a select few

title: Equitable Innovation: Delivering on AI’s Health Equity Potential Presented by Sanofi

speakers.name: Tanisha M. Sullivan
speakers.title: Head, External Engagement & Health Equity Strategy

speakers.name: Dr. Nicol Turner Lee
speakers.title: Director, Center for Technology Innovation (CTI) and Senior Fellow, Governance Studies

description:
Emerging technology, like artificial intelligence, is reshaping healthcare at record speed with great potential to advance health equity, but for communities that have long faced barriers to quality care, the promise of AI comes with urgent questions: How do we build trust in emerging technology?  Who is the technology built for? Whose data trains it?
At its core, this discussion will focus on a critical question for patients, practitioners, technologists, and communities: Will AI close, or widen, longstanding health disparities? Leading voices in health equity, technology, and policy will explore how to build trustworthy AI systems, ensure representative data, and hold institutions accountable for equitable innovation.
Join us for a candid conversation about power, progress, and the future of healthcare access in the age of artificial intelligence and what it will take to get it right for underserved communities.

title: The New Sales Playbook Presented by Sierra
description: Reggie Marable went from professional football player to working at a call center to building the sales engine behind Sierra, one of the fastest-growing enterprise AI companies in the world. In this talk, he shares how AI is changing the entire selling motion — from prospecting to closing deals — and how being adaptable and willing to learn is more important than ever.

title: Future Ready Workforce: Driving Engagement, Reskilling, and Global Innovation Presented by GE HealthCare
description: Participants will leave with a clearer understanding of what it takes to prepare a workforce for AI-driven change—and how People and Technology leaders can work together to build skills, enable adoption and strengthen the talent pipeline.

title: Care For The Culture: Content Creators, Biotech Innovators & the Future of Sexual Health Presented by Gilead Sciences

speakers.name: Youssef Idelcaid
speakers.title: Executive Director and Head of the AI Research Center

description:
What happens when caring for the culture, content creation, and cutting-edge biotech come together?
The Black community remains disproportionately affected by HIV and other STIs, and creators have real power to help change how we talk about sexual health. At the same time, AI is transforming how people engage with healthcare and wellness, opening new opportunities across both industries.
This conversation brings together voices from content creation, STEM, biotech, and community engagement to explore the latest innovations in HIV and sexual health, the growing influence of digital creators, and how both are shaping what’s next.

title: Cybersecurity Meetup Presented by Progressive
description: Come join other security professionals, engineers, ethical hackers, and aspiring practitioners and grow your networks. Exchange insights on emerging threats, career growth, and the future of cybersecurity while building meaningful relationships with peers across the industry.

title: Executive Lounge Hours
Expo Hall Hours
How to Implement AI in Nursing Workflows

speakers.name: Vanessa Riley
speakers.title: CEO, American Board of Nursing Artificial Intelligence Founder, KhonsuAI & VytalFlow AI President, Global Nursing AI Alliance
speakers.company: Global Nursing AI Alliance, Khonsu AI

description: AI is reshaping how nurses work across inpatient, ambulatory, and virtual care settings. This session examines practical applications, including clinical documentation automation, decision support tools, patient monitoring, and workforce optimization. Vanessa Riley covers how AI can reduce administrative burden and improve care coordination, and what nurses and healthcare leaders need to know to integrate these tools responsibly.

title: STOCK UP!: A Hands-On Wealth-Building Workshop
description: Larry Jones started driving Uber in 2016 to build a stake he could invest with. Today, nearly 700,000 people follow his market breakdowns, and his Traffic Trader system is taught to thousands through Money Moves. . This is not a lecture on why you should invest. Larry will explore how he reads charts while walking the room through the exact reads he makes before entering a position: where momentum is real, where it is noise, and how he sizes risk. Attendees leave with a process they can run themselves.

title: The Portfolio Life

speakers.name: Larry Quinlan
speakers.title: Fortune 500 & Private Equity Company Board Director
speakers.company: Former Global Chief Information Officer, Deloitte

description: The operating role built your expertise. Now build with it. Larry Quinlan spent decades running global technology strategy at one of the world's largest firms, then turned that knowledge into advisory work, coaching, and a multi-industry portfolio of influence. This session is the playbook for executives ready to move from one title to many.

title: Reducing Maternal Morbidity Through Inclusive Design

speakers.name: Dr. Dineo Khabele
speakers.title: Mitchell & Elaine Yanow Professor and Chair, Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology

description: Maternal morbidity in the United States continues to rise, and clinical interventions alone have not closed the gaps. Dr. Dineo Khabele will explore real-world examples of how inclusive design principles, applied through culturally responsive care models, multidisciplinary collaboration, and data-informed redesign, can improve detection, engagement, and outcomes in obstetric care across diverse patient populations.

title: The AI Supercomputer on Your Desk Presented by Connection
description:
NVIDIA GB10 + Lenovo ThinkStation PGX
From experimentation to real business outcomes
Explore how NVIDIA GB10 is enabling practical AI innovation, from local LLMs and intelligent agents to computer vision and robotics.

title: Open Mic: Idea Hour with Brandon Z. Hoff
locationLabel: Product & Innovation Stage (Exhibit Hall C&D (1st Floor))
description: Brandon Z. Hoff founded RUDI (Responsible Use of Digital Intelligence) and has taught hands-on sessions for AfroTech’s AI Edge series. In this Idea Hour he is your live AI advisor. Bring one of three things: a business you run where AI might help but you are not sure how, a product you want to build without an engineer, or an AI-powered product idea. Pitch it, and he will tell you how far AI can take you, what you may be missing, and the first step to take.

title: The Leadership Playbook: Managing & Mentoring Talent in Big Tech Presented by Uber
description: Navigating a career in Big Tech requires more than just technical expertise - it demands strategic leadership, intentional mentorship, and operational resilience. In this fireside chat, Tony West sits down with Keir Gumbs to talk about managing high-performing teams, building sustainable networks and succession planning.

title: Main Stage Doors Open
Assemble your AI team with Buzz Presented by Block
description:
(Bring a laptop)
With most AI tools, you work with one assistant in one chat. Buzz offers a different model: people and specialized AI agents working together in the same room.
In this hands-on lab, you’ll assemble an AI team with several different roles, then guide it through a practical challenge. You’ll set the direction, follow the handoffs, review each agent’s contribution, and decide what to move forward with. Along the way, you’ll learn how to give agents clear responsibilities, share context across a team, and keep human judgment at the center of the work.
Buzz is an open source, self-hostable workspace built by Block, where humans and agents collaborate with visible identities and shared history. No prior AI experience is required. Whether you’re an engineer, designer, founder, student, or AI-curious builder, you’ll leave with a practical approach to turning a group of agents into a team.

title: Accountability and the AI Economy with Congresswoman Ayanna Pressley
description: Congresswoman Ayanna Pressley has spent her career making sure policy reflects the people most affected by it. Now she turns that lens on AI: from data center environmental impact and bias in financial services to workforce displacement and the race to adopt AI without guardrails, this fireside examines who governs these systems and what leaders in the room are responsible for right now.

title: Connection Helix: GB10 in the Wild: Real-World AI Use Cases Presented by Connection

speakers.name: Rai Basharat
speakers.title: CNXN Helix: Fractional Chief Data & AI Officer | Enterprise AI Strategy, Platforms & Governance

description:
Discover real-world enterprise use cases where private, high-performance AI compute delivers measurable business value.
See what’s possible today, what challenges remain, and how GB10 bridges experimentation and production-ready AI.

title: Equity by Design: How Engineers and Physicians Evaluate Bias in Clinical AI
description: Health equity in AI isn't something companies can check once and move on from. It depends on AI developers and physicians working side by side. Dr. Félix Manuel Chinea takes attendees inside Doximity's approach to evaluating bias in Doximity Ask. He covers how Doximity's physicians and the teams developing the models defined bias together, created a daily Health Equity Score, and turned findings into model improvements. Real case studies show what gets caught, why it matters and how it gets fixed. Attendees leave with a framework any health tech company can adapt.

title: Founders Meetup
description: A focused networking experience crafted for emerging founders and small business owners navigating growth and innovation. This session offers an opportunity to exchange insights on brand development, funding, and scaling with intention. Designed for entrepreneurial minds ready to build and collaborate.

title: Clinical Operations,  Policy & Care Delays
description: Care delays are among the most consequential and preventable drivers of poor health outcomes. In this fireside conversation, Tamiko Foster and Aparna Ahuja examine how operational workflows, prior authorization bottlenecks, reimbursement constraints, and regulatory complexity contribute to patient harm, and where redesign and policy reform are already improving timeliness and equity of care.

title: What National Health Institutions Can Actually Do For You
description: Michellene Davis moved a $30 billion state budget before she took over National Medical Fellowships, which funds underrepresented students through medical school. Brandi Freeman leads the National Medical Association. Money, credentials, access to patients. Attendees will leave knowing what each institution funds, endorses, or adopts, how those calls get made, and who to contact first.

title: AFROTECH™ Insiders Meetup in Partnership with The Gathering Spot
description: The AFROTECH™ Insiders Meetup is an exclusive gathering for members of the AFROTECH™ Insiders community. This event creates space for meaningful connections, authentic conversations, and collaboration among some of the most innovative leaders in tech and culture. Attendees will gain access to unique insights, resources, and opportunities designed to elevate their careers and ventures. More than a networking event, the meetup celebrates community, innovation, and the collective power of AFROTECH™ Insiders.

title: Grounded, Then Cleared
locationLabel: AfroTech Authors Pavilion Presented by Penguin Random House
description: Captain Nia Gilliam on resilience, career reinvention, and rebuilding after a defining moment changes everything you've built.

title: State of Black Business - Earn Your Leisure x Morgan DeBaun AMA
description: Join Earn Your Leisure for a live podcast recording featuring Morgan DeBaun as they reflect on a decade of building, funding, and scaling AFROTECH™. Through candid stories and hard-earned lessons, they'll share how they've created opportunities, built a thriving ecosystem, and expanded access for the next generation of builders and founders. As AFROTECH celebrates 10 years of innovation, this conversation offers a look back at the milestones that shaped the journey and the opportunities that lie ahead

title: Discover & Preserve the Stories that Shape US Presented by Ancestry

speakers.name: Lisa Glover-Gardin
speakers.title: Vice President, Associate General Counsel, Privacy and Product and Chief Privacy Officer

description:
Every family has stories worth preserving, but many begin with only a few names, photos, or memories. In this session, attendees will learn how to transform what they already know into a living family history using Ancestry's powerful genealogy tools and AI-powered discovery experience.
Led by Ancestry CTO Sriram Thiagarajan, VP & Chief Legal Officer Lisa Garden Glover, and Principal Product Manager Breana Jones, this session will guide participants through building the foundation of a family tree, uncovering historical records with AI, and preserving family photos, documents, and stories for future generations. Along the way, attendees will gain insight into the importance of responsible AI, privacy, and trust when preserving their family's legacy.

title: Your Next Opportunity Starts With a Skill Presented by Microsoft
locationLabel: Product & Innovation Stage (Exhibit Hall C&D (1st Floor))
description:
The future belongs to people who can learn as fast as technology evolves.
Join Microsoft for a live demo of AI Skills Navigator and Learning Agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot, and discover a new way to build skills for an AI-powered world. See how personalized guidance can help you identify opportunities, uncover the skills that matter most, and take meaningful steps toward your career and learning goals.
Whether you're exploring AI for the first time or building on existing expertise, you'll experience how AI can transform learning from a collection of courses into a personalized journey of growth.
Come curious. Get inspired. Leave with a plan.

title: Demystifying Publishing Presented by Penguin Random House
description: Tamira Chapman, CEO of Storehouse In A Box and Publisher of Storehouse Voices, and Associate Publisher Porscha Burke discuss pathways for writers ready to pursue traditional book publishing projects. Whether you're just beginning to chronicle your story or have self-published several titles, you'll hear insights on preparing and positioning your work, identifying optimal publishing partners, and what to expect along the way. One of the newest imprints under the Penguin Random House umbrella, Storehouse Voices is a dynamic publishing outlet offering unrepresented and over-worthy storytellers opportunities for a traditional publishing experience, and in this session, you’ll learn how the imprint came to be and how it hopes to serve the world of culturally resonant storytelling.

title: Global Summit Begins
Blood, Bytes & Bias: Clinical Trials and AI-Driven Research

speakers.name: Travis Cleaves
speakers.title: Deputy Director of Research Informatics and Data Science
speakers.company: American Society of Hematology Research Collaborative

description: Medical AI is being trained on data that too often leaves Black patients out. Clinical trial participation, representative datasets, and accountable research infrastructure are not optional equity measures. They are the foundation for AI that can accurately diagnose, treat, and save Black lives. With Sickle Cell Disease and Multiple Myeloma as anchors to his argument, Travis Cleaves breaks down how EHR systems and trial pipelines feed medical AI, where Black patients go missing, and what the gap costs.

title: Building Trust & Confidence Across Healthcare
description: Trust is the foundation of effective healthcare delivery, yet it remains fragile across patients, providers, and systems. In this fireside conversation, Dr. Vindell Washington shares how healthcare leaders can sustain trust while scaling data, technology, and new care models. He covers transparency, data stewardship, interoperability, and patient engagement as pillars for confident adoption of AI and digital health tools.

title: Empowering Small Businesses with AI Presented by OpenAI
description:
Small businesses are where AI's promise gets tested. This conversation brings together the organizations, investors, city and community leaders who back founders every day to discuss what's keeping small businesses from adopting AI, what they actually need from these tools and how to make sure the economic opportunity reaches the communities that need it most.
Facilitator: Cliff Worley, Founder & AI Consultant at AI Playtime

title: HBCU Alumni Meetup
description:
An elevated networking experience celebrating the legacy, leadership, and cultural impact of HBCU alumni. This gathering creates space for connection, recognition, and community among those shaping the future of tech and more through historically rooted excellence.
Afrotech Conference Badge Required

title: Keeping Satellites Alive: A Hands-On Demo
locationLabel: Product & Innovation Stage (Exhibit Hall C&D (1st Floor))
description: Julia Weber, Space Manufacturing Engineer at Planet Labs, will bring a real SuperDove satellite to the AfroTech stage, giving attendees a rare, hands-on look at the hardware behind the world’s largest commercial Earth observation fleet. Drawing on her background as a Space Systems Engineer, where she managed orbital health and real-time execution in space, Julia will break down how satellites are controlled from Earth to capture daily imagery for climate monitoring, disaster response, and food security. Now helping build Planet's next-generation manufacturing capabilities, she brings an end-to-end perspective from cleanroom build to orbital operations, inspiring greater representation and highlighting the wide range of careers shaping the future of space

title: Reframe Haiti: Media, Money, and Market Power
description: Using Haiti as a global case study, this session examines how culture can become market power. The conversation moves beyond crisis narratives to examples in film, sports, fashion, Marvel storytelling, World Cup qualification, and digital media, showing how creators, technologists, athletes, and diaspora networks can turn visibility into investment, partnerships, ecosystem growth, and more informed engagement with emerging markets.

title: The Man of Many Fathers
locationLabel: AfroTech Authors Pavilion Presented by Penguin Random House
description: Comedian, writer, and television host Roy Wood Jr. on his book and what family and fatherhood teach us about showing up.

title: Book Signing with Earn Your Leisure
Live Financial Planning Workshop: What's Everyone Else Doing With Their Money? Presented by Betterment
description: You'd never book a planner just to ask "is this normal?" In this room, that's the whole point. 300 people in tech, at your level and the next one up, saying out loud what they're doing with their money and what they're still figuring out. Evol Greaves, Betterment's VP of Engineering, hosts and goes first with his own story: how his thinking about money changed as his career grew, and the questions he still has. Kyle McBrien, CFP, brings the five things he thinks about for everyone. Your questions go in at check-in and get asked for you, no names attached. Then small groups with the planners.

title: Africa's Fintech Opportunity
description: Africa's fintech ecosystem is building financial infrastructure the rest of the world is watching. Mobile money, digital lending, and cross-border payments are being reimagined at scale, and the builders driving it are redefining what's possible. Zekarias Amsalu has accelerated 100+ African startups and helped unlock $400M in growth capital. This session explores what's being built and how diaspora professionals can actively participate.

title: Make It Ours: How Outsiders Rewrite the Rules of Luxury
locationLabel: AfroTech Authors Pavilion Presented by Penguin Random House
description: Pulitzer Prize-winning critic Robin Givhan on how Virgil Abloh, with no formal training, became the first Black artistic director in Louis Vuitton's 164-year history, and what his rise says about race, taste, and who gets to define a brand.

title: Running for Elected Office as a Corporate Professional
description: Knowing how the rules around money are made gives you an advantage most people never develop. Pierre Whatley has spent his career inside those decisions at the Federal Reserve, on the House Financial Services Committee, and as Staff Director of a Senate subcommittee. Then he went from advising candidates to being one. This conversation breaks down how financial policy shapes your access to capital and your ability to build wealth, and what it takes to move from understanding the system to shaping it, including running for office while holding a corporate career.

title: The HCP Skill Stack for 2030
description: The skills that made a great clinician in 2015 are not the same ones needed in 2030. Dr. Shannon Barnes Martin examines the emerging competency stack healthcare professionals will need to navigate AI, digital transformation, and shifting care models, covering digital fluency, data literacy, clinical expertise, and leadership, and offers a practical framework for building those competencies into workforce development.

title: AFROTECH™ Conference | Out Of Office Lounge
description:
Out Of Office is headed back to AfroTech for the third year in a row to bring you a true OOO experience.
This time, Out Of Office is teaming up with Blavity, Jordan Brand, and Fidelity Investments to bring you The Breakroom, a two-day lounge experience across the street from the convention center.
Trust us, this isn’t your average lounge.
Jordan Brand is taking over the entire second floor with free merch customization and exclusive retail access to some of their most sought-after drops.
Fidelity Investments is bringing a photo booth activation and opportunities to connect with their hiring team in a laid-back setting.
Plus:
Free food & drinks while supplies last
Games & good company
Activations from Discover Gidi & Buggg
DJ sets from some of your favorites
Come find your people, kick back, and stay for the energy. This will be one of them ones!
RSVP HERE for Access.

title: Future of Work Meetup Presented by Gusto
description: Great talent is everywhere, and the future of work belongs to the teams who go find it. Join the Black with Gusto leaders, including Chief Compliance Officer LaSalle Vaughn and Head of Subscription Sales Peter Lezama, for a few quick words on building strong teams where everyone belongs. Then stick around to network, mingle, and meet some good people.

title: Smart Cities 101
description:
A city isn't smart simply because of the technology it deploys. It's smart because of what that technology enables people and communities to do.
Smart Cities 101 explores how aligning community priorities, technology, entrepreneurship, and capital can transform municipal challenges into economic opportunities.
Join Kasheef Wyzard, National Director of Economic Opportunity at Dream.Org; Jordan Taylor, CEO of SynergyGrid; and Dr. Reginald Parker, CEO and Founder of Green Power Ventures—pioneers of the Smart Cities Alliance—as they introduce a practical framework for building smarter cities that create jobs, attract investment, strengthen local economies, and expand community ownership.
Because building smarter cities isn't just about adopting technology. It's about organizing the people, partnerships, and resources needed to move from conversations to deployable projects—and ensuring communities share in the value created.

title: Building a Venture-Backable Company
locationLabel: Product & Innovation Stage (Exhibit Hall C&D (1st Floor))
description: Profitable is not the same as venture-backable. Investors who have backed some of the most category-defining companies in tech break down what they are actually looking for at the earliest stages: how they evaluate founders, why most companies cap their own upside, and how creators and bootstrappers can build for scale without giving up their edge. Walk away with a capital strategy that meets you where you are.

title: How Small Nations Are Winning Big in Global Tech Infrastructure
description: Bermuda’s transformation into a critical hub for global digital infrastructure offers a blueprint for competing on the world stage. Minister Lightbourne will share how regulatory clarity, technical excellence, and strategic positioning helped secure Google’s Nuvem and Sol subsea cable infrastructure projects. The session highlights how smart governance accelerates trust, attracts billion-dollar investments, and enables small nations and underrepresented communities to win major tech partnerships through transparency, strong systems, and community engagement.

title: American Heart Association Accelerator Program - Solutions Showcase
description:
This HealthStack Solutions Showcase will convene senior leaders across healthcare, technology, policy, and investment for a curated solutions showcase and executive feedback forum.
This session will spotlight six sponsor-supported grantees, each presenting innovative approaches to addressing systemic health disparities in Black communities.

title: The Algorithm Changed Who Gets a Microphone
locationLabel: AfroTech Authors Pavilion Presented by Penguin Random House
description: Gatekeepers versus direct-to-audience: how creators across books, television, fashion, and social are building audiences and owning them.

title: Vision First. Strategy Second. A Financial Planner's Framework for Turning Income, Equity, and Opportunity Into More Intentional Choices Presented by MassMutual
description: You're building a career, a business, a side venture, or maybe all three. Is your financial strategy built for you? This session is a practical conversation about creating greater access to the financial knowledge, perspective and resources that can support wealth building on your terms. Join experienced financial planners Achu Akum and Matthew Bennett with moderator Darin Florenz to explore how income, equity, benefits, taxes and life priorities can work together. Walk away with 10 practical questions for navigating opportunities and trade-offs and creating a financial roadmap shaped by your vision, your circumstances and what matters most to you.

title: Global Summit Ends
Technology, Policing & Public Trust
description: As cities adopt public-safety technologies, their decisions shape policing and community trust. Featuring René Peters Jr., Sr. Product Manager, AI/XR/Telecom at NVIDIA, and moderated by Kandia Milton, Dream.Org’s Government Affairs Director, this fireside chat explores how cities approach these tools, what safeguards deployment requires, and how to balance innovation, public safety, and community trust.

title: Third Spaces & Building Real Community with The Gathering Spot
description: Ryan Wilson and TK Petersen, co-founders of The Gathering Spot, share how they built one of the country's most influential membership communities and why intentional third spaces are essential for career growth, creative collaboration, and surrounding yourself with people who elevate you.

title: Closing the AI Trust Gap in CX
locationLabel: Product & Innovation Stage (Exhibit Hall C&D (1st Floor))

speakers.name: Yemi Akisanya
speakers.title: Vice President of Culture and People Experience

description: Customer-facing AI is scaling fast. Trust is becoming the limiting factor. In this fireside chat, Zendesk Chief Legal Officer Shana Simmons breaks down what it takes to build AI that customers and frontline teams will actually adopt, built around three requirements: mandatory transparency, operational explainability, and real accountability. For technical leaders deploying AI in high-stakes customer moments.

title: Dating with Strategy
locationLabel: AfroTech Authors Pavilion Presented by Penguin Random House
description: Relationship coach Anwar White (1.5M+ followers) on dating with intention in the age of apps, built on discernment and authenticity.

title: Future of Product & Design Meetup
description: AI is changing how we research, prototype, and ship, basically overnight. Come trade notes and meet with PMs, designers, researchers, and builders who get it. What’s working? What’s breaking? What’s actually worth the hype?

title: Writing the Next Chapter of Black Prosperity

speakers.name: Frank Tramble
speakers.title: Vice President for Communications, Marketing and Public Affairs

speakers.name: Kweli Zukeri
speakers.title: Assistant Vice President of Web Innovation and Strategy

description:
Every generation inherits a different set of opportunities and obstacles. Ours has inherited one of the greatest technological transformations in modern history. The question is not simply how Black communities participate in this moment, but what we must build to ensure innovation becomes a catalyst for lasting prosperity.
In this thought-provoking conversation, Frank Tramble, Vice President for Communications, Marketing and Public Affairs at Duke University, and Brandon William Jones, Founder and CEO of Gravy Wealth, explore the future of Black prosperity from two connected perspectives: the institutions with the reach and influence to shape opportunity, and the individuals and communities working to turn that opportunity into ownership and generational wealth.
Moderated by Kweli Zukeri, Associate Vice President of Web Innovation & Strategy at Howard University, the discussion will examine how institutional influence, education, capital, and entrepreneurship intersect to shape economic opportunity for Black communities. From expanding access and building trust to developing financial confidence and creating pathways to ownership, the conversation will explore what it takes to move beyond participation in the innovation economy toward building lasting economic power.
Rather than focusing on technology itself, this session challenges attendees to consider the broader ecosystem required to convert today's breakthroughs into tomorrow's generational impact. What responsibility do institutions have to create the conditions for prosperity? How can Black talent and innovation translate into greater ownership? And what decisions must we make today to ensure future generations inherit more than opportunity?
Attendees will leave with a deeper understanding of the relationship between institutional influence and individual economic mobility, practical perspectives on strengthening pathways to ownership, and a renewed sense of their own role in shaping the next chapter of Black prosperity.

title: Data Centers & Community Solutions

speakers.name: Alexis Cureton
speakers.title: E2 Fellow, Principal Community Partnerships and Grants Consultant

speakers.name: Johnelle Brown
speakers.title: Operations Chief of Staff and Vice President of Operations

description: What should communities expect from the infrastructure powering AI? Mayor Derrick Rainey of Wrightsville, Arkansas, representing AAMA; Walter Powell, CEO of UnityCloud; Alexis Cureton, E2 Fellow and Clean Energy Consultant; and Johnelle Brown, Operations Chief of Staff and VP Operations at the American Clean Power Association (ACP), join moderator Jonathan Polo, Sustainability at CoreWeave. They will examine energy demand, affordability, environmental impacts and community ownership. The conversation will address costs, trade-offs and community concerns, and the commitments needed to deliver lasting local value.

title: The Sound of Change with Vic Mensa
description: Vic Mensa has never separated the music from the business, the activism, or the ownership. From building 93 Boyz to reclaiming his story through Halfrican, he turns culture into equity, at home and across borders. This conversation unpacks what it takes to own your work, own your narrative, and build something that lasts.

title: From Viral to Published
locationLabel: AfroTech Authors Pavilion Presented by Penguin Random House
description: Reesa Teesa on turning a single viral story into a platform, a brand, and a book, and what it takes to own an audience.

title: Leading the Next Era of Space Exploration
locationLabel: Product & Innovation Stage (Exhibit Hall C&D (1st Floor))

title: Who Owns the Upside
description:
As billions flow into clean energy, AI infrastructure, and the modernization of our cities, a critical question remains: Who owns the upside? How do we ensure communities aren't simply hosting infrastructure investments, but sharing in the wealth they generate?
Dr. Reginald Parker, President of Freedmen Green Bank & Trust; Jordan Taylor, CEO of SynergyGrid; and Kasheef Wyzard, National Director of Economic Opportunity at Dream.Org, will facilitate a conversation exploring how Community Benefit Agreements, Community Benefit Trusts, and innovative ownership models can transform infrastructure investment into lasting economic opportunity.
From local jobs and entrepreneurship to community ownership and wealth creation, the discussion will examine how cities, developers, and capital partners can build projects that deliver returns for investors and the communities they serve.

Financing the Build
description:
Great ideas don't build infrastructure. Aligned capital, capable partners, and clear pathways to implementation do. How do cities move promising solutions beyond pilots and into financeable, scalable projects that deliver lasting community value?
Join Ryan Taylor, climate technology investor and energy finance expert, and Noble Madu, Partner at Plente Group, with John Payne, Chief Financial Officer at Dream.Org, moderating.
Drawing on experience across utility-scale renewable energy, venture capital, investment management, and institutional partnerships, panelists will explore how public, private, and philanthropic capital can work together to accelerate infrastructure development. From project finance and commercialization to value capture and access to capital, the conversation examines the financial structures, strategic relationships, and investment opportunities needed to move from concept to construction—while ensuring economic returns translate into meaningful benefits for communities.

title: OURstory, NOT HIStory

speakers.name: Sean Wilson
speakers.title: National Director of Organizing and Partnerships

description:
Who tells a community's story shapes who gets to define its future. As cities evolve through technological innovation, infrastructure investment, and economic development, whose voices are shaping the vision—and whose stories are being left behind?
Join J Paul Johnson, Founder of BlackEverything.com, and Michael Hawthorne Jr., Co-Founder of Klean Energy Kulture, with Sean Wilson, National Director of Organizing and Partnerships at Dream.Org, moderating.
Together, they'll explore storytelling as essential infrastructure—a tool for preserving community history, elevating lived experience, building collective power, and influencing how cities invest and grow. From cultural preservation and climate storytelling to community organizing and economic opportunity, this conversation examines how residents can move beyond being subjects of change to becoming authors of their communities' futures.
Because building smarter cities isn't just about what we build. It's about whose stories, voices, and visions guide the way.

title: Turning Internal Expertise Into AI-Proof Personal Brands
locationLabel: Product & Innovation Stage (Exhibit Hall C&D (1st Floor))
description: Layoffs in tech hit Black workers first and hardest. AI is accelerating that curve. Meanwhile, the professionals landing board seats, advisor roles, and next jobs before the old one ends all share one thing — a public personal brand they built while still employed. But Black corporate professionals are navigating landmines their peers aren't. Compliance reviews that hit harder. HR policies enforced selectively. The respectability tax. The real, rational fear of retaliation for speaking publicly about work. Roxy built Sloefy — a personal branding platform for corporate professionals — because she lived this. In this session she will walk through the Personal Brand Map framework she uses with clients, show attendees how to extract workplace expertise without crossing compliance lines, and leave them with a 30-day plan they can start Monday morning. This is not a "build your personal brand" talk. It's a leverage strategy for a workforce that needs one before the layoff email arrives.

title: Pilot to Profit Innovation Showcase
description:
Cities don't just need more innovation. They need solutions they can deploy. What does it take to move promising technologies beyond the pilot stage and into real municipal contracts, commercial opportunities, and community impact?
Join Kasheef Wyzard, National Director of Economic Opportunity at Dream.Org, and Dr. Reginald Parker, President of Freedmen Green Bank & Trust, as they facilitate the culmination of the Pilot to Profit accelerator.
This showcase features founders developing solutions aligned with real municipal challenges—from energy and infrastructure to resilience, housing, and community well-being. Through direct feedback, strategic connections, and engagement with potential buyers and partners, founders are on a journey to adoption, investment, and scale.
Because the goal isn't simply to showcase what's possible. It's to turn innovation into implementation—and create economic opportunity in the process.

title: The Video Backlog: Leveraging AI to Produce More with Descript
locationLabel: Product & Innovation Stage (Exhibit Hall C&D (1st Floor))
description:
Every team is being asked for more video: marketing, training, internal comms, exec thought leadership, and beyond. The requests keep growing, but the production team doesn't, and most of the work sits in a backlog.
In this hands-on session we’ll take a rough recording to a finished video in real time. Attendees will learn the AI tools in Descript that handle the polish that used to require a professional editor, then use Underlord, Descript's AI co-editor, to apply that same work across a whole project from written prompts. You give the creative direction. The AI does the edits.
Attendees will leave with a repeatable process they can run themselves or hand to their team.
